title: The S&P 500 Is Not Enough: My 3-Stock Starter Portfolio for New Investors
detail:
The S&P 500 Is Not Enough: My 3-Stock Starter Portfolio for New Investors
John Ballard, The Motley Fool
Sat, October 3, 2026 at 1:35 PM EDT
^GSPC
NVDA
GOOG
AMZN
META

Trading disclosure

Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN), Meta Platforms (NASDAQ: META), and Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG) (NASDAQ: GOOGL) are my three-stock starter portfolio for new investors in October 2026. I think these stocks offer more long-term growth potential than an S&P 500 index fund.

The S&P 500 has delivered an average annual return of 9.98% since 1928 through 2025, according to The Motley Fool's research. All three of these tech giants have a track record of beating the market, and they're still posting the kind of growth that can sustain that outperformance.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Index funds have their place as an anchor investment. But adding a few quality growth stocks from companies people use every day is a practical way to aim for above-average returns without taking too much risk.

Image source: Getty Images.
1. Amazon's cloud growth can power the stock ahead of the S&P 500

To beat the market, I want to see a business growing revenue faster than the index's historical average annual return. Amazon is clearing that bar, with total net sales up 20% year over year in the second quarter of 2026, reaching $200 billion.

Amazon's growth is coming from multiple engines, including e-commerce, advertising, and cloud computing. For me, Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the biggest driver of potential outperformance versus the index.

Demand for artificial intelligence (AI) cloud services pushed AWS revenue up 37% year over year in Q2 2026 to $42 billion. Amazon now plans to spend roughly $220 billion this year on data center capacity and related technologies to keep up with demand.

Amazon's trailing price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio is about 20 as of Sept. 30, although its trailing earnings got a one-time boost last quarter from its investment in Anthropic. Amazon's forward P/E on 2026 earnings estimates, excluding that gain, is about 30, which is still reasonable relative to the company's growth.

The stock could dip if cloud demand cools, but over the long term, AWS could grow into a much bigger business as more enterprises adopt cloud services and use AI tools. I believe buying Amazon today and holding for at least five years will deliver superior returns.

2. Meta's advertising business is still compounding with billions of daily users

Meta ended the second quarter of 2026 with over 3.6 billion daily active users across Facebook, Instagram, Messenger, and WhatsApp. That massive user base supports an advertising business that generates nearly all of Meta's revenue each year.

title: Meta Platforms Stock Rose 25% in September. Is It Still a Buy in October?
detail:
Meta Platforms Stock Rose 25% in September. Is It Still a Buy in October?
Keithen Drury, The Motley Fool
Sat, October 3, 2026 at 1:47 AM EDT
META
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Meta Platforms (NASDAQ: META). was one of Wall Street's best-performing stocks in September. It rose 25% during the month, turning around what had up to that point been a down year for the stock.

The major catalyst in the quarter was the launch of Meta Muse, an AI agent built for everyday use for the masses. This completely shifted the AI narrative around Meta's stock, causing the market to shift from bearish to bullish.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

But with the calendar flipping to October, will the market still love the stock?

Image source: Getty Images.
Meta finally released a monetizable AI product

Previously, the biggest complaint investors had about Meta Platforms as an AI investment was that it seemed to be giving everything away for free, despite investing hundreds of billions of dollars into building AI data centers. With no obvious payoff for those investments in sight, investors were left scratching their heads about when and where the profits would come from.

This caused investors who were familiar with Meta's failed metaverse vision to experience déjà vu. As a result, the stock wasn't highly valued. But all of that flipped shortly after the launch of Muse.

Muse is one of the first AI agents built for everyday use. The AI agent can be tasked with multistep activities such as building a schedule, checking calendars, or booking travel on your behalf.

While it is technically free to use, the free tier has a relatively low monthly usage cap. Meta is betting that many people will find Muse useful enough that they will start burning through their tokens and eventually decide to pay for a subscription tier with a much higher ceiling. If that happens, the subscription services could lead to strong revenue and profit growth, which investors love.

The market sees the vision and is buying into it, which is why the stock had such a fantastic September. But what's ahead for October?

Late this month, Meta Platforms will report its third-quarter results, and Muse will likely be one of the primary topics of discussion. Investors will likely hear more about early adoption numbers and the long-term vision for this product. If the market likes what it hears, the stock could end the month strong. However, Meta no longer has the "cheap" factor going for it. While it was trading at bargain levels for some time, its September rally drove it back to a normal valuation range.

title: Why the iShares Semiconductor ETF Gained 11% in September
detail:
Why the iShares Semiconductor ETF Gained 11% in September
Jeremy Bowman, The Motley Fool
Fri, October 2, 2026 at 10:05 PM EDT
SOXX
NVDA
META
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Shares of the iShares Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ:SOXX) were moving higher last month, continuing a long winning streak for semiconductor stocks.

The sector bounced higher in the middle of the month as investors responded to the positive reviews of Meta Platforms' new Muse AI personal agent, which could herald a new era for AI as personal agents gain adoption.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

If Muse and peers like Instinct are the next chatbots, then it will drive another wave of demand for CPU, memory, and other semiconductor components.

That news helped push the ETF up 11%, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence.

As you can see from the chart below, much of the gains came in the middle of the month as the Muse news drove the sector higher.

SOXX data by YCharts

Chip stocks rally again

Nearly all of the top chip stocks were winners last month, benefiting from the Meta news.

The SOXX's top five holdings include Nvidia, Micron, AMD, Broadcom, and Intel. Three of those stocks were up double digits, with Intel gaining 34%, AMD up 30%, and Micron climbing 11%. Meanwhile, Broadcom fell 5%, and Nvidia gained 3%. That makes sense since AMD and Intel are both CPU makers, and therefore have the most exposure to agentic AI. Broadcom and Nvidia have limited direct exposure to products like Muse.

Elsewhere, the Federal Reserve raised interest rates by 25 basis points. Higher interest rates tend to pressure growth stocks like semiconductors, but the sector was able to continue to rise.

Concerns about AI safety aired by Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and others also failed to derail the rally. Towards the end of the month, the top AI leaders met at the White House with President Trump to discuss safety issues, though no meaningful regulation came out of the meeting.

Image source: Getty Images.

What's next for the SOXX

We're just two days into October, and the SOXX is already up 3.6% for the month. Chip stocks jumped Thursday after a strong earnings report from Micron, which said that tight supply conditions in memory would last at least into 2028, showing the AI boom would continue.

On Friday, stocks jumped on a cooler-than-expected employment report, which makes an interest rate hike less likely when the Fed meets at the end of the month. Though it may seem counterintuitive for stocks to rise on weak job growth, investors are more concerned about the impact of interest rates, at least until there are clear signs of an economic slowdown.

title: Why AMD Stock Jumped 30% in September
detail:
Why AMD Stock Jumped 30% in September
Jeremy Bowman, The Motley Fool
Fri, October 2, 2026 at 8:50 PM EDT
AMD
NVDA
META
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Shares of Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) were among the winners last month after the diversified, fabless chip company rode a surge in CPU stocks following the launch of Meta Platforms' new Muse personal AI agent. AMD also announced an acquisition and benefited from some positive analyst commentary.

As a result, the stock finished the month up 30% according to data from S&P Global Market Intelligence.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

As you can see from the chart below, most of the stock's gain came in the middle of the month as the market reacted to Muse.

AMD data by YCharts

Is CPU demand about to soar?

CPU stocks, including AMD, Arm, and Intel, all soared in the middle of September on signs that Muse could become the next blockbuster product in AI. AI agents like Muse rely on the computing power of CPUs, so the companies that make them, like AMD, Intel, and Arm, all moved higher.

In less than a month, Muse has been downloaded 5 million times, and it's become the most downloaded app on the App Store and Google Play. It's also received rave reviews, showing that AI agents could be the next wave of AI, potentially driving a surge in demand for CPUs.

The other major news out on the company was its acquisition of World Labs at the end of the month for $8.2 billion in stock. World Labs is an AI model and research lab that will bring a team of researchers and model experts to AMD, helping it develop AI hardware, software, and systems. The all-stock deal is also a smart way for AMD to take advantage of its elevated stock price.

A number of Wall Street analysts also raised their price targets and upgraded the stock in the quarter, citing increasing demand for AI compute and the expansion of the CPU market from AI agents.

Image source: Advanced Micro Devices.

What's next for AMD

AMD is now a trillion-dollar company, and it has been one of the biggest winners since the stock market dip in March, as the stock has tripled since then.

AMD is one of the most diversified chip companies on the market with strong positions in both CPUs and GPUs, giving it multiple ways of capitalizing on the AI boom. It's the #2 maker of PC and server CPUs and the #2 player in the GPU market.

While significant profit growth is now priced into the stock, the business is accelerating, and it's poised to capitalize on increasing demand for CPUs.
